exceptions.reason: A ring has no ordered sequence to arrow along, and its marks are already one tab stop each: every legend row is a real button, so a keyboard user reaches a slice directly instead of walking to it. A roving cursor is the answer for an axis, and substituting one here would replace N direct stops with N key presses. Focus on a row moves the same hover the pointer does, so the emphasis and the centre percentage follow the keyboard either way.

additions.reason: Every legend row is a real <button type="button">, so sliceActivate is reachable by keyboard and the row answers Enter and Space without the component binding either. It replaces a <div> with a click handler inside a tabindex="0" group, which let a keyboard user scroll the legend and activate nothing (WCAG 2.1.1). The group keeps its role and aria-label and drops its own tab stop: a focusable child scrolls its overflow ancestor into view, so the stop the container carried is dead once the rows can take focus. Focus moves the same hover the pointer does, so the ring emphasis and the centre percentage follow the keyboard. This is ahead of the pattern rather than a divergence from it -- figure-with-data-table does not require it.
